Most of them, Your Honours will have seen put into the binders. Your Honour, that would be made, please, 2646. Now, Your Honour, can I then ask for these to go on the ELMO so that Your Honours can see what's happened here? The first map that Mr. Inayat prepared is showing overall the religious destruction within the municipalities based on the evidence we've called as opposed to what is in the indictment, because Your Honour there are certainly when we get to the Rule 98 we will certainly be conceding that there are a number of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: My problem, in inverted commas, here, I do recall when we had the expert witness dealing with the destruction of religious buildings and religious properties, he had himself, if I remember well, drawn up a map showing Catholic, Muslim mosques and other buildings of a religious nature where they teach, and we already had a map of this.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the difficulty was is we limited him because of the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Oh, I see.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: To a few municipalities and this one shows all the municipalities about which we have called evidence. I wonder if that could just be put on the ELMO so that Your Honours can see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I understand now. This will be 2647, no?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It will, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours will be provided --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's the colouring, I'm afraid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We can't see anything when --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I can distinguish mosques from churches but that's about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: If we can just look at Sanski Most, can we focus on that a little bit more.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, please speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Apparently not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: The translator has asked Ms. Korner to speak into the microphone, she doesn't have her headphones on so we couldn't hear that and secondly let me just say that I don't know why we are going through this little exercise, because Your Honours can look at it at your leisure, and frankly I have a lot of things to do before I leave here tomorrow and I'd like to leave as soon as we can, Your Honour. I think that we are just wasting time doing this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman wants to leave, of course Mr. Cunningham is still here. However, I think it's important because this is a question of what the public see, Your Honour, as well, and we are ending the, effectively, the Prosecution case for Mr. Brdjanin, so I think it's important that we deal with these.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. And the explanation that you have given after my question justifies actually your doing so, so let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, that's -- yes, as you say, 2647. The next map is the exhumation sites and I wonder if that could just briefly be put up on the ELMO? Thank you. Thank you very much. And that will then be 2648. The next map, to become 2649, is the detention camps. Thank you. And finally, 2650 is a map showing the sites where, Your Honour, killings took place, that is, not individual killings but effectively more than one person or two people. Thank you very much, usher, that's fine. 2650 that will become. Your Honour, the two CD-ROMs, I'm afraid there is a slight problem and they have to be redone and they will be available. May they be made in absentia, 2651? I'm told they are here. So... Your Honour, the next set of documents is a statement of an investigator, Mr. Ackheim, which produces the photographs of the Mount Vlasic area, where the killings took place in August of 1992. Your Honour, I think, perhaps, if the statement could be made 2652 and the actual photographs 2652.1?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the item 28 is a statement of Mr. Grady relating to photographs of the Velagici school site. Your Honour, can I ask that these be put on the ELMO just to show you and Mr. Ackerman what they are intended to show? Your Honour, these were satellite imagery provided by the American embassy, can we just go back, you'll see, Your Honour, marked - it's not the clearest unfortunately on this photograph - but you can actually make out the building in this marked area. It's quite difficult to see, I accept, and then that was 1990, and then if you go to the 21st of August, 1992, so this was about a month or so afterwards, the killings, we say, it's just trees, that there is no building. I think that's much clearer than the earlier photograph. Thank you. Your Honour, that -- could the statement be made 2653 and the actual photograph 2653.1? And sorry, and there are some other photographs of the Velagici which I won't bother to put up. Then there is a statement of Ms. Ward relating to the provenance of intercepts, how we received them. So that would be P2654. The -- there is a Rule 92 bis statement of the witness who Your Honour may recall was too ill, and I think it's been allocated a number already. So that's already in. Then there is a further statement of Mr. Grady, that relates to how he obtained the original diary from Sanski Most. So that's P2655. Your Honour, the next or the last item is the video now on CD-ROM of the speech of Mr. Karadzic that I put to the last witness. We played part of it in opening but we never seem to have formally exhibited it, so that's what that is. And there will be a transcript of it as well attached. 2656. And the transcript, please, then will be 2656.1. Your Honour, finally I think there is the Kotor Varos binder of exhibits, which we raised yesterday, whether Mr. Ackerman had ever written any objections to it and he's not sure and nor are we but I don't think so. In any event, on the same terms --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think we had admitted it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You had admitted it, had you? Ms. Gustin didn't seem to have the record of it. Perhaps the Registry can assist. Was the Kotor Varos binder of documents admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Any case, let's not waste time. If it hasn't, it's being admitted now. So for us, this whole procedure is a matter of formality. At the end of the day we will do the filtering exercise that requires to be done.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Your Honour, then, amazingly enough, just over 18 months, since we began this case, subject to the witnesses that Your Honour knows about in August, the Prosecution formally closes its case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Ms. Korner, and I think it is my duty here in open court to express my gratitude and appreciation for all that you have done. Sometimes under very heavy pressure from the Chamber to bring your case to an end. You have done it most efficiently, I must say, and for this, I must express, I feel I'm duty-bound to express our appreciation, our sense of gratitude, on behalf of Judge Janu and Judge Taya who is not here, but who I consulted yesterday before she left and she agrees completely that we should make this declaration in public. I'm sure that Mr. Ackerman will be equally responsible and equally efficient in conducting the Defence case, which will commence if and when the decision on the Rule 98 bis opens up the Defence case, because that stands to be seen obviously. And we don't know exactly where we are heading as yet, not having seen the motion itself and not having seen your response. So I think these past 18 months have, if nothing else, have shown one thing: That I think we tried on our part to ensure that there was a fair trial all the time. And I think I owe it to you publicly that you followed suit and that in the whole process, you were as fair as you could possibly be, being the Prosecution. In my country we say the Prosecutor is the accused's best friend, and you have fulfilled your role, Ms. Korner, together with all the other prosecuting officers that have helped you in this case. You have fulfilled this role most responsibly I must say and for that too I want to show you my appreciation.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: On behalf of all of us, Your Honour, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. So we'll reconvene, I take it, on the 27th of August, with the testimony of Mr. -- whoever his name is, whatever his name is, if he is certified fit to attend. If not, do I take it that we are bringing forward the cross-examination -- the other witness by one day or will the other witness come definitely on the 28th?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: He will definitely -- the second witness, will come definitely on the 28th, that's the organisation that's been done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, as I say, I hesitate because I thought you were referring to the second witness. I think the first one wasn't protected but even so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thought so, but anyway --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But, Your Honour, we are making inquiries to see what the situation will be about the first witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But please do let my legal officer, senior legal officer, keep him informed of any progress along those lines.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we will certainly do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If necessary, even if we can't have the testimony of that witness on the 27th, if necessary, it may be the case of convening the case for a short while for an hour or so on the 27th just the same to make sure that everything is in order and that we can proceed timely with the Rule 98 bis, your response would still be in the pipeline then. But Mr. Ackerman's Rule 98 would have been filed in the meantime. So we will take matters up from that moment, even if that witness is not brought forward to continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, one of the things we are going to try and investigate is if because of his condition he's unable to travel back to this Court, whether we could set up a videolink, if not for that date, for another date. But we are hoping we will be able to get him back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But if you do so, Ms. Korner, and we reserve judgments on that after having heard Mr. Ackerman, our wish is that you do so in a timely fashion.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Not to have it delayed unduly, because it would impact definitely on the Defence rights to have everything in place before they can proceed with --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, as Your Honour may remember, he's actually gone on holiday, which is what we hoped would perhaps soothe the troubled spirit. So we may have some difficulty in contacting him but obviously if that's what it comes down to, we will try and make as speedy arrangements as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Do you wish to make any statements, Mr. Ackerman, before we pack our bags and go home for a break?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, only to say, Your Honour, that we have gone through a pretty difficult patch here since the 19th of May, and I think we've all made very serious efforts to get through it. It's not been easy. But we got there and I think we got there well, and I appreciate -- I want to express my appreciation to the Court for the Court's appreciation of some of the difficulties we were facing on our team.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I also in this regard want to add to my previous statement that your behaviour, your conduct, throughout has also helped considerably to make the work of this Chamber lighter than it would have otherwise been had you been obstructive in your approach, which certainly you haven't been. So we leave it at that. May I wish you all a good break. I know that we will all be working. I have already packed the documents that I have to take with me, but at least I will be reading those on the beach and not in chambers or in the -- or in my apartment here in The Hague and that I can read at my leisure and pleasure without the pressure of work that we usually face here when we are in session and doing other things as well that fall within our responsibility. I wish you nice holidays and we will reconvene as agreed on the 27th. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 11.23 a.m., to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 27th day of August, 2003
